 Judgment

In this appeal filed under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C, accused has challenged his conviction and
sentence for the offence punishable under Section 376 (2) (l) of I.P.C. Vide the

impugned judgment and order, the trial Court has sentenced the accused to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years and also pay fine of Rs.50,000/- in default to undergo simple imprisonment for six months.
The trial Court further ordered that in the event of realization of the fine amount, the same shall be paid to the victim as compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the trial Court.
3. A charge sheet came to be filed against the accused alleging that prosecutrix who is aged about 21 years is mentally retarded.
Accused is neighbour of prosecutrix who is the daughter of complainant Mahadevi Jamadarakhani.
Accused was in the habit of speaking to the prosecutrix and sending her to shop to get him beetle leaves-nuts and pay her Rupee 1 or 2 as reward.
In this way, prosecutrix used to attend the accused for getting beetle leaves-nut.

Misusing this situation and knowing fully well that the prosecutrix is mentally retarded and she is not in a position to know what is happening and also not in a position to resist, on 21.07.2016, at around 10:30 a.m, accused call the prosecutrix under the pretext of getting him beetle leaves-nuts and took her inside the cow shed belonging to him bearing No.518/1 and squeezed her breasts and pulled down her underwear and inserted his finger into her vagina and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 376 (2) (l), IPC.
4. In respect of the incident, complaint is filed by Smt. Mahadevi Jamadarakhani - the mother of prosecutrix.
Based on it, the concerned police registered the case in Cr.No.238/2016 and conducted investigation.
The prosecutrix and accused are subjected to medical examination.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C by the Judicial Magistrate with the assistance of a Psychiatrist.
The statements of witnesses were recorded.
The spot Mahazar was drawn.
The sketch of the scene of occurrence was got prepared.
The clothes of the prosecutrix as well as the accused were seized and sent for chemical examination.
After completing the investigation charge sheet was filed against the accused.
5. During trial the accused did not have the benefit of bail.
6. Accused pleaded not guilty to the charges framed against him and claimed trial.

sentences.text: In support of prosecution case in all 21 witnesses are examined as PW-1 to 21.
Ex.P1 to 54, MOs-1 to 15 are marked.
8. During the course of his statement, the accused has denied incriminating evidence led by the prosecution.
9. He has not chosen to lead any defence evidence.
10. Vide the impugned judgment and order the trial Court convicted the accused and sentenced him as detailed above.
11. Being aggrieved by the same, the accused has filed this appeal, contending that the impugned judgment and order of sentence is illegal, perverse and opposed to law, facts and evidence on record.
It is it illegal, erroneous, one- sided, and purely based on conjectures and surmises.
The trial Court has committed error in blindly accepting the evidence of PW-10, 11 and 12.
It is a clearly a cooked up case by the complainant.
During the course of his cross- examination, PW-11, the Medical Officer has admitted that the victim is able to understand common things and she is a person of sound mind.
Such being the case PW-10 could have given voluntary statement before the Court.
11.1 The trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that there is improvement in the evidence given before the Court and the same cannot be taken into consideration.
The prosecution has failed to prove the ingredients of Section 376 (2) (I) IPC.
There is inordinate delay in filing the complaint and the same is not taken into consideration by the trial Court.
The prosecution has failed to prove the allegations against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
There is no judicial application of mind.
Viewed from any angle the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable and prays to allow the appeal, set aside the impugned judgment and order and set the accused at liberty.
12. On the other hand, the learned High Court Government Pleader supported the impugned judgment and order and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

13. Heard elaborate arguments of both sides and perused the record.
14.
Thus, it is the definite case of the prosecution that the prosecutrix though aged 20 years is mentally retarded and is not having mental maturity of her age.
For this reason, accused person was utilising her services as though she is a child and making her to fetch him beetle leaves-nuts from the shop and in return used to tip her Rupee 1 or 2.
This was being done since long.

However, on the ill-fated day i.e., on 21.07.2016, under the pretext of sending her to the shop to get beetle leaves-nuts, accused called the prosecutrix and took her inside the cow shed belonging to him.
There, he squeezed her breasts and pulled her underwear and inserted his finger in her vagina.
When she cried, hearing the commotion, her mother Mahadevi Jamadarakhani, her neighbour Suvarna Uppin, Rathnavva Angadi and sister of prosecutrix Savithri Kurubetta rushed to the spot.
Seeing them accused ran away.
Prosecutrix narrated as to what happened.
After the father of prosecutrix returned home from the land, complainant brought the incident to his knowledge and after consulting elders of the village, they chose to file complaint.

Of course there is evidence of Investigating Officer i.e., PW-21 Raghavendra Hawaldar, who has deposed that on 23.07.2016, he visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar as pointed out by the complainant and prosecutrix in the presence of witnesses.

According to the prosecution, at the time of incident, she was collecting water from the public tap, which is situated opposite to the place of incident and PW-1 - Mahadevi Jamadarakhani and PW-14 - Savitri Kurubetta, the mother and sister of prosecutrix were inside their house.

Her statement given before the jurisdictional magistrate i.e., PW-19 - Maruthi.K, is treated as Examination-in-chief as provided under Section 164(5-A) (b) of Cr.P.C and she is subjected to cross-examination by the defence in the presence of Physiatrist PW-11 Dr.Rajendra Katte.

Learned counsel for accused submitted that in the light of this admission and having regard to the fact that the prosecutrix is mentally retarded, no reliance could be placed on her evidence.

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that though the prosecutrix is mentally retarded, as noted earlier the extent of her mental retardation is 'Moderate' and her IQ is 45.
It is nobody's case that the prosecutrix is unable to understand anything.

The very fact that accused used to utilize her services to certain his errands indicate that her intelligence was that of a child and it was taken advantage by the accused to send her to the shop for getting beetle leaves- nuts and was rewarding her by paying Rupee 1 or 2.
The over all examination of testimony of PW-1, 9, 10 and 14 prove the allegations against the accused.

The testimony of the prosecutrix is supported by the evidence of PW-1, 9 and 14, who are though not strictly speaking eye witnesses to the actual incident, they have reached the spot immediately on hearing the cries of the prosecutrix and seen accused running away from the cow shed belonging to him, wherein the prosecutrix was found crying.

21.3 The testimony of PWs-1, 9, 10 and 14 is corroborated by the evidence of PW-19 Maruthi K,
learned Judicial Magistrate, who has recorded the statement of the prosecutrix in the presence of PW-11 Dr.Rajendra Katte, Physiatrist.

At the first available opportunity the statement of the prosecutrix is recorded and it corroborates with the prosecution case and the testimony of PW-1, 9 and 14.
21.4

As evident from the cross-examination of PWs-1, 9, 10 and 14, neither the family members of the prosecutrix nor PW-9 Rathnavva Angadi, an independent witness are having any ill will or motive to falsely implicate the accused.
They all living in the same area along with the accused and as such natural witnesses.
They have no reason to falsely implicate the accused.
In fact it is elicited through their cross-examination that the accused is a respectable resident of that area and he was treating the prosecutrix as his daughter.
They have admitted that there are no similar allegations against the accused earlier to the present case.

Having regard to the nature of the offence in question, it cannot be expected that accused was committing such offence day in and out and for that reason to accept the contention of defence that accused has not committed the alleged offence.
21.5 The accused has not attributed any motive for PWs-1, 9, 10 and 14 to falsely implicate him.
On the other hand, it is alleged that the relationship of accused with his brother and his family members is not cordial and at their instance, accused is being falsely implicated.
Of course, they have denied the said suggestion.

Though it has come in the evidence of PW-9 that at the time of alleged incident,
the wife and daughter of brother of accused namely, Mahadevi and Sridevi were in their house, but she has specifically stated that they did not come out of their house. Probably being the relative of accused or on account of their stained relationship with the accused, they chose to remain inside despite the commotion outside the house.
However, the defence has failed to prove that at the instance of the brother of accused and his family, he is falsely implicated.
Dr. Farhat M. Khan (wrongly typed as Farath) has examined the prosecutrix and given report as per Ex.P-31.
Her evidence reveal that she found a fresh injury at 10 o'clock on the libia menora and a scratch.
She also observed a fresh tear at 6 o'clock on the hymen.
They were fresh.
During her cross examination, though she has conceded that she has not noted the age of the injury but explained that fresh injury means within 24 hours.

sentences.text: Her evidence is required to be appreciated in light of the testimony of the other witnesses.

Of course, PW-12 has also referred the prosecutrix to PW-11 - Rajendra Katte,
Psychiatrist.
23. At this stage it is relevant to refer to the definition of 'Rape' under Section 375 I.P.C.
Prior to the amendment dated 03.02.2013, the term 'Rape' was defined as when a man has sexual intercourse with a woman.

However, as per the amendment a man is said to commit rape if he- (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b) inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (c) manipulates any part of the body of a woman so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of such woman or makes her to do to with him or any other person; or (d) applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions:-
Firstly - xxx Secondly - xxx Thirdly - xxx Fourthly - xxx Fifthly - With her consent when, at the time of giving such consent, by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication or the administration by him personally or through another of any stupefying or unwholesome substance, she is unable to understand the nature and consequences of that to which she gives consent.
24.
Of course, in this case there is no consent.

Thus, the act committed by the accused which is proved by the prosecution comes under the definition of 'Rape', as defined under Section 375 I.P.C.
25.
Based on the complaint of the mother of the prosecutrix, the concerned police have registered the case and taken up investigation.
The incident took place at around 10.30 a.m.

It has come in the evidence of PW-6 Rudrappa Jamadarakhani, the father of the prosecutrix that at the time of incident, he had gone to the land and returned around 12.00 noon and came to know about the incident.
After bringing this fact to the notice of PW-7 and CW-14, he, complainant and prosecutrix went to the Police Station and lodged the complaint.
In fact, PW-7 has also deposed that after coming to know about the incident, he advised the parents of prosecurtix to file complaint.
26. PW-8 Basavaraj Jamadarakhani is the nephew of PW-6 Rudrappa.

Thus, the prosecution has proved lodging of the complaint.

PW-18 R.R.
Bannur has assisted the Investigating Officer in the investigation.
As discussed earlier PW-20 Ninganagouda Patil has received the complaint, registered the case and transmitted the FIR to the Court, with the assistance of PW-18 R.R.Bannur, Head Constable.

PW-16 Shivabasappa Kajgar,
Head Constable has carried the FIR and handed it over to the judicial Magistrate.
PW-15 Smt.Shobha Bhosle, PSI has recorded the statement of prosecutrix as per the directions of the Investigation Officer.
While PW-20 Ninganagouda Patil, has conducted the investigation, PW-17 Ishwar Jinnavvagol and PW-18 R.R Bannur, Head Constable have assisted him in the investigation.
PW-21 Raghavendra Hawaldar, CPI has conducted further investigation including arresting of accused, subjecting him to medical examination and filed charge sheet.
The evidence of these witnesses prove the investigation.
Except suggesting that a false complaint is filed, at the instance of persons inimical towards the accused, nothing much is elicited through the cross- examination of these witnesses.

27. Appreciating the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the trial Court has rightly come to the conclusion that the allegations made against the accused are proved beyond reasonable doubt.

When the offence established against the accused comes under Section 376(2)(l), the minimum punishment prescribed is rigorous imprisonment for a term of 10 years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that persons natural life and shall also be liable to fine.
Taking into consideration the allegations proved against the accused, the trial Court has imposed minimum punishment of 10 years.
Learned counsel for accused submitted that the accused has suffered paralysis and is under treatment.

Having regard to the nature of the offence committed by the accused and the fact that minimum sentence is imposed,
there is no scope for interference by this Court, despite the fact that the accused has allegedly suffered paralysis.

28. In the result, the appeal fails and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal filed under Section 374 (2) Cr.P.C by the accused is dismissed.
(ii) The impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 19.07.2018 in S.C.No.96/2017 on the file of VIII Addl.District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi, is confirmed.

6 injury sustained by her which resemble a person trying to have forcible sexual intercourse, the Medical Officer has given the report that there was sexual intercourse immediately prior to the examination.
Thus, the act committed by the accused which is proved by the prosecution comes under the definition of 'Rape', as defined under Section 375 I.P.C.

Taking into consideration the allegations proved against the accused, the trial Court has imposed minimum punishment of 10 years.
Having regard to the nature of the offence committed by the accused and the fact that minimum sentence is imposed,
there is no scope for interference by this Court, despite the fact that the accused has allegedly suffered paralysis.
opennyai_summary.decision:
When the offence established against the accused comes under Section 376(2)(l), the minimum punishment prescribed is rigorous imprisonment for a term of 10 years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that persons natural life and shall also be liable to fine.
28. In the result, the appeal fails and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal filed under Section 374 (2) Cr.P.C by the accused is dismissed.
(ii) The impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 19.07.2018 in S.C.No.96/2017 on the file of VIII Addl.District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi, is confirmed.
(iii) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court record along with copy of this judgment forthwith.
